titulo: The tag comes back to the counter
subtitulo: Check price and fit, ask the exchange rule before paying, then return with the receipt and tag
frasePiso: You can turn a product you can see into a verified choice — price, fit, exchange condition and the right evidence for the return.

steps.pt: Recall the artifact that closed B14. A restaurant receipt verifies one payment; a shop receipt may need to travel back with the product. Ask for it again before the shopping scene begins.

steps.promptPt: Recall B14. The card payment is complete. Ask for the receipt. Speak now.
steps.es: ¿Me puede dar el recibo, por favor?
steps.pinyin: meh PWEH-deh dahr el reh-SEE-boh por fah-BOR
steps.pt: Can you give me the receipt, please?
At a clothing shop, point before you name. Esta camisa makes one visible item the centre of the question; the price becomes a return you can ask to see.
How much does this shirt cost?

steps.promptPt: A shirt has no visible price. Point to it and ask the cost. Speak now.
steps.pt: How much does this shirt cost?
It costs six hundred pesos.
The label says your usual size, but the garment itself is the evidence. Ask for a larger size, then ask to try it on. Size systems and brands vary; fit wins over the letter on the tag.
Do you have a larger size?

steps.promptPt: The shirt on the rack is tight across the shoulders. Ask for a larger size. Speak now.
steps.pt: Do you have a larger size?
Yes, here you are.
Can I try it on?

steps.promptPt: The larger shirt is in your hand. Ask whether you can try it on. Speak now.
steps.pt: Can I try it on?

steps.es: Sí. Los probadores están al fondo.
steps.pt: Yes. The fitting rooms are at the back.
steps.tts: Sí. Los probadores están al fondo.

steps.pt: The second shirt hangs loose. Do not translate a size chart. Ask for the direction the garment needs to move: una talla más chica.
Do you have a smaller size?

steps.promptPt: The shirt now hangs too loose. Ask for one size smaller. Speak now.
steps.pt: Do you have a smaller size?
Yes, I’ll bring you one.
The third size works. Close the choice with me llevo esta: this visible one, not a catalogue of colours or sizes.
I’ll take this one.

steps.promptPt: This size fits and you want the shirt in your hand. Say you will take this one. Speak now.
steps.pt: I’ll take this one.
Perfect.
Fit is not the same as a defect, so do not assume the exchange rule. Before paying, ask whether you can change it if the fit fails later, then ask how many days the store gives you.

steps.es: ¿La puedo cambiar si no me queda?
steps.pinyin: lah PWEH-doh kahm-BYAHR see noh meh KEH-dah
steps.pt: Can I exchange it if it doesn’t fit me?
steps.tts: ¿La puedo cambiar si no me queda?

steps.promptPt: Before paying, ask whether the shirt can be exchanged later if the fit is wrong. Speak now.
steps.es: ¿La puedo cambiar si no me queda?
steps.pinyin: lah PWEH-doh kahm-BYAHR see noh meh KEH-dah
steps.pt: Can I exchange it if it doesn’t fit me?

steps.es: Sí, con el recibo y la etiqueta.
steps.pt: Yes, with the receipt and the tag.
steps.tts: Sí, con el recibo y la etiqueta.

steps.pt: How many days do I have to exchange it?

steps.promptPt: The store accepts the exchange with receipt and tag, but you still need the deadline. Ask how many days you have. Speak now.
steps.pt: How many days do I have to exchange it?
You have thirty days.
The next morning, the fit is wrong under real movement. The tag is still attached and the receipt is in your hand. Ask for another size; the clerk asks for the two artifacts the store named.
I want to exchange it for another size.

steps.promptPt: You return with the shirt. Ask to exchange it for another size. Speak now.
steps.pt: I want to exchange it for another size.
Do you have the receipt and the tag?
Yes, here they are.

steps.promptPt: The clerk asks for the receipt and tag. Put both on the counter and answer. Speak now.
steps.pt: Yes, here they are.

steps.es: ¿Cuánto cuesta esta camisa? ¿Me la puedo probar? ¿La puedo cambiar si no me queda? Quiero cambiarla por otra talla.
steps.pinyin: KWAHN-toh KWEHS-tah EHS-tah kah-MEE-sah. meh lah PWEH-doh proh-BAHR. lah PWEH-doh kahm-BYAHR see noh meh KEH-dah. KYEH-roh kahm-BYAHR-lah por OH-trah TAH-yah
steps.pt: Shadow price, fitting, policy and exchange.
steps.tts: ¿Cuánto cuesta esta camisa? ¿Me la puedo probar? ¿La puedo cambiar si no me queda? Quiero cambiarla por otra talla.

steps.pt: B15 complete. Price visible. Fit tested instead of translated. Larger and smaller sizes requested by direction. Exchange policy and deadline asked before payment. Receipt and tag preserved. The return to the counter now has a sentence and the evidence the store requested.

aprofundar.titulo: Fit, policy and evidence are three different checks

secoes.titulo: The garment outranks the size label
secoes.corpo: Brand and market labels vary. Más grande and más chica describe the direction the fit needs to move without translating a sizing system.

secoes.titulo: A fit exchange is a question, not a promise
secoes.corpo: Legal protection for a defective or misrepresented product is not identical to changing a sound product because it does not fit. Ask the store’s policy and deadline before paying.

secoes.titulo: Receipt and tag are portable evidence
secoes.corpo: The staff answer names the artifacts this particular store requires. Preserve both until the fit survives real use.
Esta camisa plants the object; me la puedo probar and cambiarla keep it alive. In a real shop, pointing is part of the sentence, not a failure.
